content:
- Overestimate near recent highs; model tends to peak too early and then drop too sharply.
- Underestimate when sentiment is strongly positive (especially >0.5) — model ignores bullish momentum.
- Overshoot after sharp spikes in sentiment (e.g., +0.73) — model reacts too aggressively, then corrects too late.
- Underreact to negative sentiment spikes (e.g., -0.70) — model fails to anticipate sharp downside.
- Mean-reversion bias: model overcorrects after strong moves, leading to premature reversal.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts consistently underestimate late-period rallies (last 5–7 days of true outcome).
- Lagged sentiment: model ignores sentiment from 3–5 days prior when it’s trending strongly — should weight recent sentiment more heavily.
- Avoid “flat” forecasts when sentiment is volatile — model underestimates volatility in sentiment-driven markets.
